clips.speaker: Bloomberg
clips.title: 彭博：超市条形码革命如何降低食品成本

subtitles.en: The barcode thing was kind of blew my mind, because as you said, I never noticed it before, how come other grocery stores or other brands don't do something similar?
subtitles.zh: 条形码的设计让我很惊讶，因为我之前从未注意过。为什么其他超市或品牌不采用类似的做法？

subtitles.en: For us, it's strictly productivity, and since we control the product and the packaging, we can put 20 barcodes if we wanted to.
subtitles.zh: 对我们来说，这纯粹是为了提高效率。因为我们控制产品和包装，所以想放20个条形码都可以。

subtitles.en: But if I'm like a hogging dozer or something, and I'm designing my box of ice cream sandwiches or whatever it is, I would be reluctant to give up some of that additional space to barcodes.
subtitles.zh: 但如果我是其他品牌，在设计冰淇淋三明治的包装时，我不太愿意把宝贵的空间让给条形码。

subtitles.en: I think so. I mean, if you're a brand, you want to talk about the products, and you would have the romance copy, and you want to tell the history of the product.
subtitles.zh: 没错。品牌方更想介绍产品，用浪漫文案讲述产品历史。

subtitles.en: I think they're more focused on that than the retailer's productivity. We're focused on the productivity so we can get the savings for the customer.
subtitles.zh: 他们更关注这个，而不是零售商的效率。我们注重效率，以便为顾客节省成本。

subtitles.en: But you're absolutely right. Adding romance copy and all those great runs on the back of the bill.
subtitles.zh: 你说得对。在包装背面添加浪漫文案和那些精彩的故事。

subtitles.en: Is that what you call it? Is that what you call it? It's called romance copy.
subtitles.zh: 你们是这么叫的吗？浪漫文案？

subtitles.en: I have often felt feelings of romance as I do have a bag of ice cream pack.
subtitles.zh: 我拿起一袋冰淇淋时，确实常常感受到浪漫。

subtitles.en: Do you ever like those things? It'll be like Bob and Joe's corn chips.
subtitles.zh: 你见过那种吗？比如鲍勃和乔的玉米片。

subtitles.en: And it's like the story will be like, Bob was working at Goldman Sachs, and realized why am I devoting my life to M&A when I could like be devoting it to like design big.
subtitles.zh: 故事是这样的：鲍勃在高盛工作，后来意识到为什么要把生命献给并购，而不是设计大包装。

subtitles.en: I always, I'm not a fan. I always think that's, I do not need romance copy and stuff.
subtitles.zh: 我向来不喜欢那种浪漫文案之类的东西。

subtitles.en: You need to know the origin story of your potato chips, Joe. Below and welcome to another episode of the AdLots podcast.
subtitles.zh: 你得知道薯片的起源故事，乔。欢迎收看本期AdLots播客。

subtitles.en: I'm Joe, why isn't all. And I'm Tracy Alley. Tracy, can't say something.
subtitles.zh: 我是乔，还有特蕾西·艾利。特蕾西，说点什么吧。

winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有特朗普/美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
